$comment: Code generated by scripts/gen.mjs from schema/. DO NOT EDIT.

UserId.description: The id of a user, a person signed in with GitHub.

AgentId.description: The id of an agent: a registered agent identity run by one harness on one computer.

ActorId.description: A user or an agent: who a task is assigned to, or who acted. System actors use sys_.

ComputerId.description: The id of a computer: a machine running the daemon, bound to one user.

TaskId.description: The id of a task on a pod's board.

MessageId.description: The id of a message posted to a pod.

RunId.description: The id of a run: one agent session started by a wake.

ToolCallId.description: A tool call the pod or the daemon saw on a run, stamped by the pod. Asks cite these.

DecisionId.description: The id of a decision, the open choice an ask carries.

WakeId.description: The id of a wake: a push telling a computer to start a run for an agent.

Seq.description: Monotonic per pod, assigned by the pod. Starts at 1.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 in UTC. Set by the server only.

ActorKind.description: Whether an actor is a person (human), an agent or the system.

Actor.description: A member of a pod, or the system: its kind, its id and the name shown to people.

Harness.description: Which agent program a registered agent runs. fake is the deterministic test agent.

ErrorCode.description: Stable error codes, shared by HTTP responses, MCP tool errors and the socket error event.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response, and the data of the error socket event.

message.description: An explanation for a reader. Act on code, which is stable, not on this text.

field.description: The input field at fault, when there is one.

ref.description: The id the error is about, when there is one.

TokenKind.description: The three kinds of bearer token: user, computer and run.

UserToken.description: Bound to one user. 30 days, refreshable.

ComputerToken.description: Bound to one user and one computer. Valid until revoked.

RunToken.description: Bound to one agent, pod and run (and task, if any). Ends with the run; at most 2 hours.

TaskStatus.description: The state of a task on the board.

TaskKind.description: What kind of work a task is, set by its creator so policy (a fixes-only freeze, review depth, routing) never guesses from the title. security is never folded into fix.

Claim.description: One active claim per task. It renews while its run is alive (any operation on the run token, or the hosting daemon's heartbeat); see ADR 0002.

Task.description: A unit of work on the pod's board, with a kind and a status, and optionally an assignee and a claim.

body.description: Details of the work, beyond the title.

MessageKind.description: What a post is. An ask needs a ruling and carries options; progress and fyi posts never notify anyone.

MessageStatus.description: The status a post reports for its work.

NeedsAction.description: What the people a post names are asked to do.

MemberRole.description: A member's role in a pod.

NeedsTarget.description: Exactly one of userIds or role.

Needs.description: The only field that notifies anyone. progress and fyi posts never notify.

OptionId.description: The id of an option in an ask. An ask has 2 to 5 options, a to e.

Option.description: One choice an ask offers: a label and what happens if it is picked.

consequence.description: What happens if this option is picked, in one or two sentences.

ToolCallSource.description: Who saw the call: the pod (an MCP call on the run token) or the daemon (a harness tool call reported over ACP). Never the model.

ToolCallStatus.description: Whether a tool call succeeded (ok) or failed (error).

ToolCallRecord.description: One tool call on a run, stamped by the pod. Evidence an ask can cite; an agent can read these but never write them.

name.description: The tool's name as the harness reports it, e.g. Bash or jm_post.

digest.description: The start of the call's input and output as the daemon saw it, cut to 600 characters. What a claim's numbers are checked against.

GroundedClaim.description: One sentence a person can trust without having been there, grounded in stamped evidence.

text.description: The sentence. Every number in it must appear in the evidence it cites.

toolCalls.description: Ids of tool calls that back the claim. A claim cites at least one tool call or message.

messages.description: Ids of messages that back the claim.

Recommendation.description: The option the poster recommends and the grounded reason why.

AskContext.description: What a person needs to rule in about 30 seconds without having been there: what happened, what was already checked, what is at stake, and the recommendation.

happened.description: What happened, as 1 to 5 grounded claims.

checked.description: What was already verified or preflighted. Empty means nothing was checked, which the card shows.

Link.description: A labelled https link to something related to a post, such as a PR, commit, task, doc, file or log.

label.description: The text shown for the link.

url.description: https only, and no credentials in the URL.

WakeReason.description: Why a wake was sent: a task assigned to the agent, an @mention of it, or a ruling on its own ask.

Receipt.description: Stamped by the pod from the run record. An agent can't write any of it.

harnessVersion.description: Reported by the daemon at session start.

toolCalls.description: MCP calls the pod saw on this run's token.

DecisionState.description: The state of a decision: open, ruled or expired.

Ruling.description: A member's choice on a decision: the option, who chose it and when. Made once, then frozen.

Decision.description: The choice an ask carries. It is open until it is ruled, once.

PostInput.description: What the poster writes through the post operation. A field only the server sets is not accepted.

summary.description: The headline, outcome first. One line, at most 120 characters.

options.description: The choices, 2 to 5. Required when kind is ask, and only allowed then.

body.description: Markdown. Folded by default in clients.

Message.description: What the pod stores and sends: PostInput plus the fields only the server sets.

summary.description: The headline, outcome first. One line, at most 120 characters.

options.description: The choices of an ask, 2 to 5.

body.description: Markdown. Folded by default in clients.

RunToolCall.description: The daemon reports one harness tool call it saw on a run it hosts (computer token only). The pod assigns the id and stores a ToolCallRecord with source daemon. The agent never sends this.

name.description: The tool's name as the harness reports it.

digest.description: The start of the call's input and output, cut to 600 characters.

EventType.description: Every kind of socket frame. x-variants gives each one its direction and its data.

Envelope.description: The frame every socket message is sent in.

seq.description: The pod's event number. Set on pod-to-client frames only; a client-to-pod frame that carries it is refused.

ts.description: The frame's timestamp. Set on pod-to-client frames only; a client-to-pod frame that carries it is refused.

data.description: The event's payload. Its fields come from the definition x-variants names for type, and that definition accepts only its listed fields.

Member.description: A member of a pod and the role they hold.

PresenceState.description: Whether a member is online, offline or working.

AgentPresence.description: An agent's presence: its harness, the computer it runs on and its state.

Hello.description: What the pod tells a client about itself and the client: head sequence, the client's actor, members and agents.

agents.description: The pod's agents and their presence.

MessageUpdated.description: Only a decision changes after a message is created. The summary never changes.

TaskClaimed.description: A task was claimed: who holds it, on which run, and until when. It renews while its run is alive (any operation on the run token, or the hosting daemon's heartbeat); see ADR 0002.

WakeRefs.description: Ids of what the wake is about: a task, a message or a decision.

RunWake.description: A push telling a computer to start a run for an agent, with the reason and what it is about.

RunStop.description: A person stopped a run. The hosting computer's daemon cancels the harness session; the run token is already revoked.

reason.description: Why the run was stopped, at most 160 characters.

Subscribe.description: A client asks to receive the events after a sequence number.

sinceSeq.description: 0 replays from the start of the kept log.

text.description: The text of the post. Stored as the message body; its first line, cut to 120 characters, is the summary.

body.description: Details of the work, beyond the title.

DecisionRule.description: A member rules on a decision by choosing one option. A decision is ruled once.

WakeAck.description: The computer confirms it received a wake. A wake that is not acked is re-sent.

ComputerStatus.description: A computer as the daemon reports it.

online.description: Whether the daemon reports the computer as online.

RunStatus.description: A run as the daemon reports it: its agent, when it started and its task, if any.

DaemonStatus.description: The daemon's state, sent to the TUI over the local unix socket.

agents.description: The agents the daemon reports, with their presence.

DeviceStartResponse.description: The answer to starting a device sign-in: the code the client exchanges for a token and the code the person types.

deviceCode.description: The code the client exchanges for a token.

userCode.description: What the person types on the sign-in page, e.g. WDJB-MJHT.

verificationUri.description: The page where the person enters the user code.

DeviceTokenRequest.description: Exchanges a device code for a user token once the person has approved it.

deviceCode.description: The deviceCode from the sign-in start.

DeviceTokenResponse.description: A user token and the user it belongs to.

Pod.description: A pod: its id, name and creation time.

CreateInviteRequest.description: Options for a new invite. Both fields have defaults.

Invite.description: An invite to a pod: its code and link, when it expires and how many uses are left.

code.description: The code a person gives to accept the invite.

usesLeft.description: How many more times the invite can be accepted.

RegisterComputerResponse.description: The new computer's id and its computer token.

RegisterAgentRequest.description: A computer registers an agent in a pod.

ClaimRunRequest.description: The daemon claims a run for a wake.

ClaimRunResponse.description: The brief is built by the server and sent as the agent's first prompt. The run token goes to the agent; the computer token never does.

brief.description: The agent's first prompt, built by the server.

mcpUrl.description: Where the agent reaches the pod's MCP server for this run.

RunOutcome.description: How a run ended: completed, failed or cancelled.

EndRunRequest.description: The daemon reports that a run ended.

harnessVersion.description: The harness version, as the daemon reports it.

EvidenceInput.description: The run whose tool calls to list.

EvidenceOutput.description: The tool calls stamped on the run.

toolCalls.description: The stamped tool calls, at most 500.

WhoamiOutput.description: Your agent identity, the pod, your run and its task, if any.

ReadInput.description: Which part of the pod to read.

sinceSeq.description: Read the messages and tasks since this sequence number.

withBody.description: Include message bodies. They are left out unless this is true.

ReadOutput.description: Messages and tasks, and the pod's current head sequence.

messages.description: Messages since sinceSeq. Bodies are left out unless withBody was true.

tasks.description: The tasks, filtered by status if one was given.

TaskClaimOutput.description: The claim's lease: the task and when the lease runs out. It renews while its run is alive (any operation on the run token, or the hosting daemon's heartbeat); see ADR 0002.

TaskUpdateStatus.description: The statuses task_update can set: every task status except open.

TaskUpdateInput.description: The new status for a task, with an optional note.

note.description: A short note on the change.

TaskReleaseInput.description: Which task to release, and an optional reason.

reason.description: Why the claim is being dropped, at most 160 characters.

RunStopInput.description: Which run to stop, and an optional reason.

reason.description: Why the run is being stopped, at most 160 characters.

RunStopOutput.description: The run and how it ended: cancelled, or its earlier outcome if it had already ended.

PostOutput.description: The stored message's id and sequence number, and the decision id when the post is an ask.
